sentences.text: Revenue went from effectively zero in FY2020 to $5,387 million in FY2025, a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [F2][F7][D342].
The step change came in FY2022, when revenue jumped 2914.5% to $1,658 million on first deliveries of 19,412 vehicles [F4][D83][P67].
Growth then decelerated sharply, from 167.4% in FY2023 to 12.1% in FY2024 and 8.4% in FY2025 [D135][D187][D239].
The loss narrowed every year after FY2022, with operating income improving from $-6,856 million to $-3,585 million and gross profit turning positive at $144 million in FY2025 [F23][F26][F14].
In FY2025 Software and Services contributed 21.6pp of the 8.4% revenue growth, while Automotive subtracted 13.2pp [D323][D239][D316].

Software and services revenue rose 221.7% to $1,557 million, 28.9% of revenue, on vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for the Joint Venture plus remarketing and repair [D322][S26][D321][P18].
Automotive revenue fell 14.6% as deliveries dropped 9,332 vehicles, partly from expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025 [D315][P22].
The Volkswagen Group relationship alone contributed 15.4pp of growth and 15.5% of revenue in FY2025 [D281][D279].
Operating costs grew 6.9% against 8.4% revenue growth, so incremental operating margin was 264.7% [D258][D239][D265].
Gross margin reached 2.7% in FY2025, its window high, against a window median of -45.8% [F19][D331][D332].
Operating margin improved 27.8pp to -66.5%, still far below the -1.6% autos peer median [D253][F31][D344].
Cost of revenue fell 15.0% and drove 26.8pp of the margin bridge, as fewer vehicles were produced and raw material and conversion costs fell [D255][D267][P21].
SG&A subtracted 0.5pp as go-to-market expansion raised payroll and stock-based compensation [D269][P13].
Net margin of -67.7% diverged from operating margin because other expense included a $186 million securities litigation settlement [F43][P10].
Operating cash flow was $-779 million in FY2025, -14.5% of revenue, against free cash flow of $-2,489 million, a -46.2% margin [F64][D227][F78][D226].
The operating outflow shrank 54.6% primarily on a significant reduction in net loss [D244][P4].
Capex rose 49.9% to $1,710 million, 31.7% of revenue and 2.18x D&A, on Normal Factory capacity expansion [D246][F71][D225][D228][P3].
Stock-based compensation of $741 million equalled 20.7% of the operating loss, so cash burn understates the economic cost [X56][D237].
Net cash fell to $1,642 million in FY2025 from $3,259 million, as cash and investments dropped 21.0% while total debt held at $4,440 million [D231][D179][D261][D230].
Net cash was still 30.5% of revenue, above the 17.8% autos peer median and in the 75th percentile of four peers [D232][D352][D351].
The current ratio fell to 2.33x, its window low, from 4.70x as current liabilities grew 64.1% [F129][D339][F128][D251].
Financing inflow of $886 million came mainly from $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group, and diluted shares rose 17.1% [F92][P2][D260].
Net losses persist in all seven years, from $-426 million in FY2019 to $-3,646 million in FY2025 [R1][F32][F38].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2][D223][D31][D67][D119][D171].
Cash and investments of $6,082 million cover 2.4 years of the latest burn [R3][D229][D236].
New electric vehicles were 67.6% of revenue and fell 12.5% in FY2025, concentrating the top line in a shrinking product [R4][D286][D287].
Product revenue members sum to 129% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so they must not be added [R6].
Whether gross margin holds above the FY2025 level of 2.7% in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the cost-per-vehicle trend [F19].
Whether operating cash flow narrows past FY2025's -14.5% of revenue toward breakeven would confirm the burn trajectory [D227].
Whether net cash stays above the FY2025 level of $1,642 million, or the current ratio falls further below 2.33x, would signal liquidity pressure [D231][F129].
